As for the crisis

Greece was borrowing small amounts of money and paying it off. Generally living as a second rate medium economy of little importance, but like most of those economies they were still trying to increase their borrowing limit as much as possible and taking on slightly excessive debt. No one would lend them too much though so they were generally stable and not going to fail. The Euro came along. To be in the Euro you had to have a certain financial strength. Many countries were excluded, and many were later added. Why? Because they didn't have the right finances, but then they worked to straighten it out and were added in. Greece was part of the 'not so good finanaces' group bu went straight into the Euro for 2 reasons.

1- "But we are europe!!! Let us in. We are historic plz"

2- Other political connections and moves that were behind the scenes

When Greece entered the Euro their economy didn't grow at an unusual rate, but their borrowing limits did because they could piggy back off the currency strength the union gave. They started a massive program of spending on its citizen in welfare programs. They were a republicans nightmare. Giving money away with no effort in investing or returns. This led to borrowing money to pay off old debts and then borrowing more to continue it's social welfare. So now we're here.

They still don't want to cut spending and they want other people to stop asking them for all of the money they borrowed.
